note: Literature characterization confirms frequent skeletal anomalies in Fliedner-Zweier syndrome specifically consist of clubfoot, scoliosis, and hip dysplasia without reports of limb reduction defects.

evidence.text: In a cohort study delineating the molecular and clinical spectrum of SCAF4-related Fliedner-Zweier syndrome, frequent skeletal findings included clubfoot, scoliosis, or hip dysplasia.

source.title: Further delineation of the SCAF4-associated neurodevelopmental disorder
source.quote: Frequent clinical findings were mild developmental delay with speech impairment, seizures, and skeletal abnormalities such as clubfoot, scoliosis or hip dysplasia.
